name: manual_1a8b54
claim: A freshly-written process doctrine can be violated by its own author within the same session it was written — always back a doctrine with mechanical enforcement (a pre-push hook, a CI check), not just documentation, or the doctrine's own authoring is not exempt from the failure mode it was written to prevent.

decisions.notes: The Post-Review Micro-Remediation doctrine's own authoring commit was pushed directly to main while a PR was still open, violating its own Phase 0 (never push to main during active review) in the act of writing that exact rule. Caught by one user question, fixed via the doctrine's own Phase 3 procedure, then closed by adding a pre-push guard + CI backstop so the same class of mistake is mechanically blocked, not just remembered.
